title: Aging Gracefully? Reliability Profiling and Temporal Forensics of Frozen and Adapted Text Classifiers
content: Selecting a text classifier using a single benchmark score can overlook temporal variation and differ- ences in how effectively confidence identifies errors. We compare frozen prompted language models with task-adapted classifiers on Yelp review sentiment and Climate stance classification, examining whether models preferred on overall predictive performance remain preferable for confidence-based automatic acceptance. We evaluate qwen2.5:3b-instruct, phi3.5:latest, TF–IDF Logistic Regres- sion, and DistilBERT across a reference period and two later historical periods. Five paired sampling seeds provide identical class-balanced evaluation cohorts across models: 500 examples per class for Climate and 500 or 1,000 for Yelp. Supervised classifiers use historical labeled data, while prompted models remain frozen. Evaluation combines predictive performance, temporal robustness, verbalized confidence calibration, and confidence-based risk–coverage analysis. Three reference-period prompt configurations assess configuration sensitivity and explicit abstention. On Climate, task-adapted mod- els are strongest: DistilBERT achieves 0.8876 within-period Macro-F1 versus 0.7124 for the strongest frozen prompted LLM, but drops by 0.0258 and 0.0170 on short- and long-distance targets. Frozen prompted LLMs perform best on Yelp: qwen2.5:3b-instruct achieves 0.9602 and 0.9601 Macro-F1 at the two Yelp sample sizes (Yelp n500 and Yelp n1000). However, in Yelp n1000, phi3.5:latest has a smaller mean within-seed Macro-F1 range across prompt configurations (0.0091 versus 0.0107), lower reference-period ECE (0.0340 versus 0.0646), and lower error at 80% coverage (0.0181 versus 0.0249) than qwen2.5:3b-instruct. Temporal forensics show stronger lexical novelty and distribu- tional movement in Climate than Yelp, but greater dataset movement does not necessarily imply greater model degradation. These findings support multidimensional reliability assessment across deployment regimes.
